definition: An API standardization activity by the Yoriito project to abstract access to vehicle signals, composed of Yoriito Signal API and Yoriito Access API.
Open source project that provides Yoriito Vehicle API and related components, defining the scope and architecture for vehicle signal access.
High-level API that abstracts  Signal API for specific use cases, focusing on usability for applications.
Shared library that implements the  Access API for applications.
Low-level application-facing API that provides access to vehicle signals based on  VSS definitions.
Shared library implementation of the  Signal API for applications.
Extended VISS protocol and message schema set tailored for  Vehicle API for accessing vehicle signals.
Central data broker server that manages the VSS data tree and mediates communication between applications and PAL.
Client library for applications to access  VISS Server using the VISS protocol.
Client library for PAL implementations to supply signals and receive actuator targets from  VISS Server.
Extended VSS signal definitions provided by  for OEMs and suppliers to derive vehicle-specific VSS trees.
Pre-configured development container environment including SDKs and toolchains for  Vehicle API.
Platform composed of multiple  components, versioned as a whole release unit.
Concept representing whether a feature or equipment physically exists and is provided by the vehicle.
Concept representing whether a feature is currently usable under given vehicle conditions, expressed as boolean.
Common error vocabulary shared across components to unify error handling for  Vehicle API.
API method to retrieve metadata such as type, unit, and range for a given signal path.
Backend C++ application that receives UI requests via gRPC and calls  Signal API.
Abstraction layer between vehicle platform and  VISS Server, converting platform-specific signals to VSS.
Text-based UI provided to operate simulator vehicle and test various signals without coding.
